From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Archipelago renewal — proposed save package (summary + ask)

Hi Jonas / Kim,

Quick background: Archipelago (large generative AI tooling customer) is up for renewal 10/15. Their usage spiked this year; they’ve requested a nonstandard renewal to offset overage and stick with Redwood rather than re-platforming. They are asking for a 25% list discount, a $45k one-time credit to cover the last quarter’s overages, and an SLA add-on (4-hr response, 99.9% monthly availability) for the next 12 months.

Attached is a short summary and the concession sheet with economic impact. Net-new ARR risk if we don’t act: likely churn or 6-month pause ($1.1M ARR exposure). Proposed deal to preserve revenue:
- Renewal: 12 months, $2.0M committed ARR baseline (down from their current $2.4M forecast)
- One-time credit: $45,000 (applied at signing)
- Discount: 20% on list across baseline (not applicable to overages)
- SLA: add the managed SLA add-on at no charge for first 12 months, subject to quarterly review

Why this is time-sensitive: procurement wants an answer by EOD 9/06 to include in their board packet. I’ve tried internal levers (coupons, usage forgiveness) but this package requires approval from deal desk + exec sign-off for the one-time credit and SLA concession.

Ask: Can we approve the proposed package as-is, or do we want to counter with a smaller credit (e.g., $25k) and a 15% discount? I recommend approving the full package to avoid a churn risk and preserve logs/data retention continuity.

Attachments: Archipelago_Renewal_Summary.pdf, Proposed_Concession_Sheet.xlsx

Thanks,
Ben

Jonas — answers below and I added procurement’s note where relevant.

1) Exposure: Confirmed with CSM (Diego Luna) — they flagged two high-churn signals: paused product roadmap and exploring another vendor for inferencing cache. If we don’t provide an immediate commercial alternative, likely 50-70% chance of churn. That’s where the $1.1M number comes from (projected 12-month revenue at risk).

2) SLA cost delta: Support estimates from ops are ~ $8k/month incremental for the enhanced SLA (on-call rotation + faster escalation) — roughly $96k annual expected ops cost. We’re offering it complimentary Year 1 in the proposed package, so ops impact is material but not prohibitive.

3) Contract protections: Yes — procurement asked for a rollback clause; we should instead add: (a) usage guardrails (cap the forgiveness to baseline + 10%), (b) a quarterly operational review, and (c) a clause that the complimentary SLA reverts to paid SLA at renewal if performance targets aren’t met.

Procurement note (from Diego): "Board wants certainty; they’ll sign if we provide the one-time credit + SLA concession. They explicitly asked for the SLA in writing in the contract. Deadline EOD 9/06."

Given the ops cost, my recommended counter if we don’t want to approve full ask: $30k one-time credit + 18% discount + complimentary SLA for 6 months instead of 12. But if leadership is willing to trade $45k credit + 12 months free SLA to prevent churn, I support the full package.

Ben
